newsitem.title: USA: U.S., N. Korea hold missile talks in NYC.
newsitem.headline: U.S., N. Korea hold missile talks in NYC.

text.p: The United States and North Korea opened on Wednesday in New York long-delayed talks on Pyongyang's missile programme, the State Department said.
"We can now officially say that the non-proliferation talks have started," spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.
The talks were to have been held in New York on May 12-13 but Pyongyang postponed them for what it called "technical reasons." Previous talks on the issue were held in Berlin in April 1996.
The U.S. negotiating team is headed by Deputy Assistant Secretary of State Robert Einhorn while the North Korean side is headed by Foreign Minstry Director Li Hyong-chol.
The United States has long been concerned about North Korea's programme of producing, deploying and exporting missiles and has sought the talks as a means to negotiate a halt in the programme.
U.S. officials have said progress on this issue is crucial to improved U.S.-North Korean ties.

Pyongyang agreed on new starting date for the new round of talks after the North and South Korean Red Cross societies last month signed an agreement under which Seoul wil supply 50,000 metric tons of food aid to the hungry North by the end of July.
According to its arch-rival South Korea, North Korea can produce about 100 Scud B and C missiles a year and so far has exported about 400 to the Middle East.

Seoul has said Pyongyang now exports about $500 million worth of Scud missiles a year and weaponry exports between 1980 and 1993 accounted for about 30 percent of North Korea's total exports amounting to $20.4 billion.
Independent experts say North Korea has been exporting plants and machinery for the production of the Scud missiles to Iran and Syria as well as technology for the development of the deadly weapons.

South Korea's 655,000 troops, bolstered by U.S. soldiers, have confronted the North's 1.1 million-strong army across the world's last-remaining Cold War border since the 1950-53 Korean War ended in an armistice.
